content:
Let’s evaluate each option in the context of exercise physiology:  

- **(A)** Ammonia is produced in repeated high intensity exercise.  
  True — ammonia production increases during intense exercise due to adenosine monophosphate (AMP) deamination.  

- **(B)** Muscle lactate accumulation does not begin until at least 5 seconds of intermittent muscle contractions have taken place.  
  False — lactate can begin to accumulate almost immediately (within the first few seconds) during high-intensity exercise, not only after 5 seconds.  

- **(C)** Muscle phosphocreatine depletion begins in the first few seconds of high intensity exercise.  
  True — phosphocreatine breakdown starts rapidly at the onset of intense activity.  

- **(D)** With an increasing number of repeated sprints the rate of accumulation of lactate in muscle declines.  
  True — due to reduced power output and increased lactate clearance/oxidation in later sprints.  

The clearly false statement is **(B)**.  

Final answer: (B)
